item.title: Oliver Tree Memorial Service to Be Livestreamed on July 25
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this special episode, where we're remembering the life and legacy of Oliver Tree, a talented artist who tragically passed away in a helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on June 14.
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: A memorial service and celebration of life has been set for Oliver Tree, scheduled for July 25 at the UCSC Quarry Amphitheater in Santa Cruz, California. Due to limited space, the event will be livestreamed for the public, with details on how to watch coming soon.
[Music fades out]
Host: Oliver Tree, born Oliver Tree Nickell, was just 32 years old when he passed away, leaving behind a legacy of music, art, and joy. His fourth studio album, "Love You Madly Hate You Badly", was released in April, and his final live performance was in São Paulo on June 6.
[Soft music returns]
Host: In an obituary released by his family, Oliver is remembered as a true artist, who saw the world as a stage for his performance art. He's described as someone who cared deeply about spreading art, joy, laughter, and love, and who wanted to create an inclusive environment where everyone belonged.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of Oliver Tree's song]
Host: Oliver's musical accomplishments include topping the Billboard Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart with his debut album "Ugly Is Beautiful", and collaborating with Robin Schulz on the hit song "Miss You". His song "Life Goes On" also reached the top 10 on the Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart.
[Music fades out]
Host: Oliver's family has requested that donations be made in his honor to the Dr. Oliver Tree's Extremely Epic Art Grant for Baby Geniuses foundation, which will support and encourage young artists to follow their dreams. You can find more information and make a donation at olivertreefoundation.com.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. We'll miss Oliver Tree, but his legacy and music will live on. Thank you for tuning in, and we'll see you next time.
